surprises.description: FSBC’s net income was $21.9 million, above the preview’s estimates of about $20.2 million at consensus and $20.6 million in its own model. Basic EPS was $0.92 versus the preview’s $0.854 diluted-EPS consensus, though those EPS measures are not directly comparable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income rose to $21.9 million in Q3 2026” and “basic EPS of $0.92.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net income” estimate: “~$20.6M”; consensus “~$20.2M.” Diluted EPS consensus: “$0.854.”

surprises.description: Total deposit growth appears far below the preview’s modeled increase of about $250 million: non-wholesale deposits rose $75.1 million while wholesale deposits fell $50 million, implying only about $25 million of net growth. The funding mix nevertheless improved, with non-wholesale deposits reaching about 96% of total deposits and noninterest-bearing deposits 25.1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-wholesale deposits increased $75.1 million while wholesale deposits fell $50 million,” raising non-wholesale deposits to “~96% of total” and noninterest-bearing deposits to “25.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated deposits of “$4.80B” in Q2 and “~$5.05B” in Q3.

surprises.description: Loan growth was weaker than the preview’s roughly $250–260 million expectation: loans held for investment increased $184.5 million. The 10%–12% loan-growth guidance for Q4 2026 and full-year 2027 also points to a slower pace than Q2’s 29% annualized growth, despite the preview’s focus on deploying the new capital and whether that pace would hold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Loans held for investment “grew $184.5 million (~16% annualized)” and management guided to “loan growth of 10% to 12% for Q4 2026 and for full-year 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q3 loans at “~$4.78B” from Q2’s “$4.52B,” and its base scenario assumed “loans +$250M.” It also noted that loans grew “29% annualized in Q2” and asked whether “the pace holds.”

surprises.description: NIM expanded more than the preview’s estimate, reaching 3.69% versus its 3.66% estimate and the base-case range’s 3.64%–3.68%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest margin expanded 6 basis points to 3.69%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “NIM” at “3.66%” and described its base scenario as “NIM 3.64–3.68%.”

surprises.description: Management provided a forward NIM range of 3.65%–3.75%, rather than explicitly guiding to at least 3.70% exiting 2026 as the preview said the buy-side wanted. The range includes 3.70% but also leaves room for a lower level.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided to a “comfortable range of 3.65% to 3.75% going forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “the buy-side wants 3.70%+ exiting 2026” and that bull commentary would include “explicit NIM guidance of 3.70%+ exiting the year.”

surprises.description: The efficiency ratio improved to 39.13%, better than the preview’s estimate of about 40% and below its stated 40% base-case level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The efficiency ratio improved to 39.13% from 40.91% in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Efficiency ratio” at “~40%” and described its base case as “efficiency ~40%.”

surprises.description: The $2.5 million provision was modestly below the preview’s $2.6–$3.0 million base-case range and its $2.8 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recorded a $2.5 million provision for credit losses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated provision at “$2.8M” and its base scenario specified “provision $2.6–3.0M.”
